before_token_paths: design-system/theme/ (predecessor @atlaskit/theme package -- global theming/colors mixins, still published to npm at v26.1.1, not deprecated)
design-system/tokens/codemods/theme-to-design-tokens/ (the codemod that performs the pre-tokens -> tokens migration itself)
notes: STEP 1 (npm): @atlaskit/tokens IS a real, currently-published npm package -- confirmed via `curl https://registry.npmjs.org/@atlaskit/tokens`. dist-tags.latest = 16.3.0, dist-tags.next = 1.4.2, earliest version on record is 0.0.13 (published 2021). STEP 2 (repo location): the research plan's assumed path `github.com/atlassian/design-system` was WRONG, and correctly flagged as unverified. Direct HTTP checks: github.com/atlassian/design-system -> 404, github.com/atlassian-labs/design-system -> 404, github.com/atlassian/atlassian-frontend-mirror -> 404. Atlassian's public frontend code does NOT live on GitHub at all. The npm package.json `repository` field for the latest version (16.3.0) resolves to `git+https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/atlassian-frontend-mirror.git` (Bitbucket, not GitHub). This was corroborated by an official Atlassian Developer Community post ('New expanded mirror repository including source for all public Atlaskit packages') describing a public, nightly-updated Bitbucket mirror of the internal 'Atlassian Frontend' monorepo containing source for every public @atlaskit npm package, organized under a /design-system folder. I confirmed this repo is live and public: `https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/atlassian-frontend-mirror` returns HTTP 200, and the Bitbucket REST API (`api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/atlassian-frontend-mirror`) returns full repo metadata (size ~668MB, created_on 2020-10-08, mainbranch master). STEP 3 (token files + migration evidence): Browsed the repo via the Bitbucket Source API and located `design-system/tokens/` inside the monorepo mirror, containing src/, codemods/, schema/, prebuilt/, docs/, figma/, CHANGELOG.md, etc. Confirmed real token-definition artifact files (token-data.json5, token-names.tsx, token-default-values.tsx) and a `codemods/theme-to-design-tokens/` directory plus `codemods/css-to-design-tokens/` and `codemods/remove-fallbacks/` -- direct evidence the documented 'pre-tokens -> tokens rollout with automated codemods' claim is real. A predecessor package, @atlaskit/theme ('Theme contains solutions for global theming, colors, and other useful mixins'), also exists on npm and is still published (latest 26.1.1, not deprecated), consistent with it being the pre-tokens system. CHANGELOG.md (4336 lines, fetched via raw Bitbucket URL) contains multiple references to the tokens migration, e.g. a link to the official guide https://atlassian.design/tokens/use-tokens-in-code#migration-to-tokens (page confirmed live, HTTP 200) and text like 'Introduced a restricted util token for use during the initial token migration.' HOWEVER -- two significant methodological problems for git-history-diffing, discovered while trying to identify before/after tags: (a) The mirror repo has ZERO git tags -- `refs/tags` via the Bitbucket API returns an empty list (size: 0), so there is no tag equivalent to the vX.Y.Z / package@version tags used for the other systems in this study, and no way to check out 'the commit for npm version 0.0.13' vs 'the commit for npm version 16.3.0' via a tag. (b) The mirror's own commit history is NOT the original commit history: every commit I sampled (most recent ~10) is an automated daily squash commit authored by a bot ('AFM_updater' / 'AFP Repo Bot (Automated)') with the generic message 'Automatic commit created <date>' -- i.e., the public mirror is a nightly snapshot sync, not a faithful copy of the internal monorepo's real commit-by-commit history. Consistent with this, the actual commit hashes cited inside the package's own CHANGELOG.md (e.g. `ecc5823dc898c`, `b1453699ad8be`) are linked to `bitbucket.org/atlassian/atlassian-frontend-monorepo` (the private internal repo, different from the public 'atlassian-frontend-mirror'), and those links 404 publicly -- confirmed directly. So: source code and migration tooling for the pre-tokens -> tokens rollout ARE real and publicly browsable, but the standard tag-based before/after diffing methodology used for the other four design systems in this study cannot be directly replicated on this repo as-is; a workaround would require picking two dated squash-commit snapshots (e.g. via the commits API filtered by date, which does work and returns real timestamped commits) rather than semver tags, and accepting that intra-day/PR-level granularity is lost. Per the task's literal fallback condition ('if NO public source repo can be confirmed to exist'), the fallback to Shopify Polaris was NOT invoked, because a real, public, browsable repo containing the tokens source and migration codemods was in fact found -- I did not investigate Shopify Polaris. This is a call the research team should revisit given the tag/commit-granularity caveats above; I flagged architecture_claim_verified as 'partial' (the pre-tokens->tokens rollout with codemods is real and documented) rather than true, and confidence as 'medium' overall (high confidence in the platform/existence facts that were directly curl/API-verified; medium/lower confidence in whether this repo, as structured, actually supports the git-diffing methodology the study needs).
